body.cap: Lee Eun-seung, CEO of DABIDA, photographed on January 9th (local time) at CES 2024 in Las Vegas, showcasing the CES 2024 Innovation Award trophy received for their remote education platform GeniClass and GeniPen. | Photo - AVING News

body.x: DABIDA Co., Ltd. (CEO Lee Eun-seung) participated in CES 2024, the world’s largest IT and consumer electronics expo held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 9th (Tuesday) to January 12th (Friday, local time).

DABIDA, an Edutech startup, gained prominence in 2020 by developing the all-in-one educational robot, ‘Genibot.’ Building on the success of its ‘Learning Interactive Management System (LIMS) engine supporting personalized learning, the company commercialized a non-face-to-face, two-way video education platform, offering differentiated learning experiences to various domestic and international customers.

DABIDA has continuously developed its education platform with independent technology and a diverse range of ICT technologies secured through global partnerships. As a result, DABIDA’s video education platform ‘GeniClass’ and the technology transforming analog writing into digital, ‘GeniPen,’ were selected for the CES 2024 Innovation Award in the Smart City category. These products received positive evaluations for their user-friendly interfaces and as next-generation solutions enhancing remote learning achievement.

GeniClass is a remote education platform based on digital text, constructed and operated through WebRTC and WebBLE, eliminating the need for separate software installation on user devices. This allows seamless execution of GeniClass on devices accessible in network and web environments without specification constraints. With real-time feedback from teachers occurring without disruption, students can efficiently and economically enhance the outcomes of remote education. Additionally, GeniClass ensures extensive compatibility through Bluetooth connectivity with various ICT devices, facilitating easy system diversification for optimized learning fields and content.

body.cap: In an interview with Alex Sirgrist, a reporter from AVING News, CEO Lee Eun-seung explained the writing tracking and recognition technology of their ‘GeniPen.’ | Photo - AVING News

body.x: GeniPen, compatible with the GeniClass platform, tracks and recognizes writing movements and content with a pen. The recognized written content is converted into digital text, enabling real-time sharing on the web for both students and teachers. Using this data, teachers can meticulously assess students’ learning tendencies, problem-solving times, attention spans, errors, etc.

GeniClass and GeniPen, as data-centric remote education solutions, contribute to efficiently enhancing academic progress. Taking advantage of these benefits, they have been applied to leading domestic education service providers such as ‘EmbassLIVE’ by Megastudy. Furthermore, DABIDA plans to launch its products in various countries, including Japan, India, Indonesia, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and Spain, in February this year. The company anticipates an expanded market exploration, drawing additional attention from multinational buyers and attendees at CES 2024.

body.cap: CEO Lee Eun-Seung of DABIDA during an interview with AVING News reporter Alex Sirgrist at CES 2024 | Photo - AVING News

body.x: CEO Lee Eun-Seung stated, “The goal of our participation in this exhibition was to create new B2B sales achievements by targeting online and offline education service providers, publishers, and customers demanding collaboration tools in the global education platform market.” He expressed expectations of entering the B2C market by refining the direction of platform localization based on insights gained at CES.

He continued, “End users benefiting from our GeniClass, GeniPen, and related technologies include all age groups, from kindergarten students to adults.” With a positive outlook, CEO Lee Eun-Seung pledged to make every effort to secure 100,000 global users this year and promised to strive for overseas market entry.

CES, the world’s largest IT exhibition organized by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), is held in Las Vegas every January, providing a comprehensive view of global technology industry trends. AVING News, covering CES for 18 consecutive years, has been selecting the best innovative products, companies, and technologies and conducting ‘BEST OF CES’ and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA’ selections. Additionally, through ‘AVING LIVE,’ they provide live coverage of CES issues.
